hooks.text: Physicists found a hidden dead star a million times faster.
One algorithm found a dead star a million times faster.
Six centuries of computing failed where ten hours succeeded.

title: The Million-Times-Faster Star Hunt
description: NASA's Fermi telescope gathered open data that choked supercomputers for centuries of processing. Borrowing math from quantum cryptography solved the search in ten hours.

beats.text: Physicists found a hidden dead star a million times faster.
beats.visual: artist's concept of a rapidly rotating pulsar with radiation beams

beats.text: Standard methods burned six hundred years of computing and found nothing.
beats.visual: Einstein@Home distributed volunteer computing screensaver displaying pulsar search

beats.text: NASA's Fermi telescope captures only sparse photons across the sky.
beats.visual: illustration of the Fermi Gamma-ray Space Telescope in Earth orbit
queries: Fermi Gamma-ray Space Telescope artist concept

beats.text: Sifting through noise used to swallow whole volunteer computing networks.
beats.visual: all-sky map of the gamma-ray universe from the Fermi Large Area Telescope
queries: Fermi LAT galactic plane gamma rays

beats.text: So researchers borrowed math designed to test quantum encryption.
beats.visual: diagram illustrating high-dimensional lattice cryptography shortest vector problem

beats.text: They mapped the search as geometry in a high-dimensional lattice.
beats.visual: geometric diagram of multi-dimensional vector grid in lattice space

beats.text: A standard computer processor found the target in ten hours.
beats.visual: photograph of a computer workstation processor running data analysis software

beats.text: It revealed a pulsar spinning 261 times per second.
beats.visual: artist's concept of an isolated millisecond pulsar sweeping magnetic radiation beams
queries: Neutron star magnetic field artist concept

beats.text: No telescope search had ever moved so fast.
beats.visual: deep space field showing distant gamma-ray sources across the Milky Way
queries: Fermi LAT galactic plane gamma rays
